description: Parameters needed to the corresponding task specification in eTaSL

from-debug_lib-version-1.0.1.description:
Library debug_lib version 1.0.1.
 Set to true to indicate that task specification comes from the library above. 
 Library description: Library with basic task specifications that may be needed when debugging communication and control of a robot
Authors: Santiago Iregui (KU Leuven), Federico Ulloa (KU Leuven)

is-move_sine_waves_jointspace.description:
Task Specification: move_sine_waves_jointspace.etasl.lua
Set to true to indicate that the task uses the task specification mentioned above. 
 Task description: Moves every robot joint along its own sine wave around its initial position (joint space, no Cartesian constraints): the target of joint i is q_i(t) = q_i(0) + amplitudes[i]*sin(2*pi*frequencies[i]*t), with t the time since the start of the task, so the motion starts at the current joint positions.
Each joint is driven to its target by a position constraint with feedback gain K_joint (with feedforward of the target velocity). No input channels are needed.
A monitor finishes the task with the event/action "exit" when the task has run for execution_time seconds.
Outputs: time and the position x_tcp, y_tcp, z_tcp [m] of the "tcp_frame" of the robot model w.r.t. the robot base (world) frame.

file_path.description: File path of the corresponding task specification

parameters.description: List of parameters needed to define an instance of the task specification

amplitudes.description: Amplitude of the sine wave of each joint, in [rad] for revolute joints ([m] for prismatic joints), i.e. the maximum deviation from the initial joint position. One value per joint, in the same order as the joints of the robot model (robot.robot_joints); the number of values must equal the number of joints. 0 keeps that joint at its initial position; a negative value inverts the direction of the wave.

execution_time.description: Duration of the task in [s]: when this time has elapsed since the start of the task, the task finishes with the event "exit". 0 makes the task finish right after it starts.

frequencies.description: Frequency of the sine wave of each joint in [Hz] (cycles per second). One value per joint, in the same order as the joints of the robot model (robot.robot_joints); the number of values must equal the number of joints. 0 keeps that joint at its initial position; a negative value inverts the direction of the wave.

K_joint.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the joint position constraints that make each joint follow its sine wave. Higher values correct tracking errors faster; 0 means only the target velocity is applied, without correcting position errors.
